ask: Announce our new store hours on LinkedIn, X, Threads and our Facebook Page: from Monday we open at 7 am. Put the full schedule as a comment on Facebook: Mon-Fri 7 am to 6 pm, Sat 8 am to 4 pm, Sun closed.

steps.why: Limits and needs for every network named, once.

posts.content: From Monday we open at 7 am. Earlier coffee for the commute, same team behind the counter.
New hours from Monday: open 7 am.
Early birds, this one's for you: we open at 7 from Monday.

contents.content: New hours from Monday: we open at 7 am. Full schedule in the comments.
Mon-Fri 7 am to 6 pm. Sat 8 am to 4 pm. Sun closed.

steps.why: The Facebook first comment is a second part on one network only, and parts are shared by every account on a post, so this is one post per network, each written fresh, in one bulk call (without it, one post with a text per network in platform_specific would do). The Facebook item has two parts: part 2 goes out as a comment from the Page, so it is aimed at the Page alone. Then poll bulk-create-status: its posts list gives the Facebook and Threads post ids for the next steps.

bulk-create-posts keeps the Facebook account but not which Page, so a brand with several Pages would publish to its primary Page. save-post with post_id and account_ids records the Page; leaving out content keeps both parts.
A setting only where it adds something: the topic people browse for this post. Name it in the reply so the user can drop it. In platform_details the tag needs use_topic_tag too.

say: Saved to Acme as 4 drafts: 1 LinkedIn, 2 X, 3 Threads (topic Coffee), 4 Facebook with the schedule as a comment under it. Nothing goes out yet. Schedule all 4? Once they're out, I'll check the live Facebook post for the comment.
never: Pasting one text and trimming it per network.
Claiming the posts will look the same everywhere.
Saying the Facebook comment is live before checking the published post.
